name: Advanced Typescript Patterns
description: This module describes advanced patterns for typescript intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.
content:
This module describes advanced patterns for typescript intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Keep typescript changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
2. Re-check edge cases relevant to typescript (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
3. When typescript decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
4. Keep typescript outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. Check that typescript terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
6. When multiple typescript strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
7. Before starting typescript work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
8. Surface known limitations of a chosen typescript approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
9. Prefer the simplest typescript approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
10. Measure before optimizing any typescript bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
11. Prefer explicit, readable typescript solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
12. When typescript guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of typescript correctness.
- Do not skip documenting typescript assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new typescript abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop typescript edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these typescript guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
